entries.title: Shared/Core update: project-file-tree

ai.title: POSIX path normalization and glob truncation warning
ai.summary: The file tree now routes relative paths through a toPosixPath helper before the ignore library evaluates them, so Windows backslash paths no longer silently bypass nested .gitignore rules and waste the file budget on build output. The SDK glob tool imports DEFAULT_MAX_FILES and appends a truncation warning when the scan hits its 10,000-file cap, telling the agent the deepest directories were not searched. Together these change how the shared core tree builder and the SDK glob tool surface results on large or Windows projects.
ai.evidence: In common/src/project-file-tree.ts, a new toPosixPath helper normalizes paths to forward slashes before feeding them to the ignore library, applied in getProjectFileTree (relativeFilePath) and isFileIgnored (relativeFilePath), replacing earlier inline backslash replacements; sdk/src/tools/glob.ts imports DEFAULT_MAX_FILES and adds a truncated warning to the glob result message when flattenedNodes.length >= DEFAULT_MAX_FILES.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show whether the toPosixPath normalization changes any existing tree output on POSIX roots, and it does not reveal which consumer first renders the new glob truncation warning to the user.

changes.what: Introduced toPosixPath and applied it to relativeFilePath in getProjectFileTree and isFileIgnored so paths fed to the ignore library use forward slashes.
Imported DEFAULT_MAX_FILES and added a truncation warning to the glob result message when the file tree hits its 10,000-file cap.

facts: Values are unconstrained on purpose: `metadata` is a free-form bag that publishers and registries nest their own structures into (skills.sh writes a `hermes:` block into every skill it serves). Requiring flat strings here rejected the whole skill over a field nothing reads.
entries.title: Shared/Core update: skill

ai.title: Freebuff skill metadata accepts nested values and clamps long
ai.summary: The Freebuff skill frontmatter schema in `common/src/types/skill.ts` now accepts `z.unknown()` values in the metadata field rather than only flat strings, allowing publishers and registries to nest their own structures such as the `hermes:` block written by skills.sh. The description field also shifted from rejecting over-long values to clamping them with a `.transform()` that slices the string at `SKILL_DESCRIPTION_MAX_LENGTH`, since an over-long description is a reason to show less of it, never a reason to make the skill unusable. Two new test cases assert this behavior with titles "accepts nested metadata a publisher or registry added" and "clamps an over-long description instead of rejecting the skill".
ai.evidence: In `common/src/types/skill.ts`, `SkillMetadataSchema` changed from `z.record(z.string(), z.string())` to `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())`, and the description field shifted from `.max(SKILL_DESCRIPTION_MAX_LENGTH)` to a `.transform()` that clamps via `d.slice(0, SKILL_DESCRIPTION_MAX_LENGTH)`.

changes.what: Relaxed the `SkillMetadataSchema` value type from `z.string()` to `z.unknown()` and clamped the `description` field via `.transform()` instead of `.max()`.

ai.title: CLI model selector stabilizes focus and layout on async access tier
ai.summary: The FreebuffModelSelector rewrite changes how the recommended model row and focus behave across collapsed, expanded, and asynchronously arriving access tiers. `showStandaloneRecommended` is true only when the list is collapsed or the tier is `limited`, so the hero card is omitted from the sectioned list in expanded full-access views, preventing it from rendering twice. `toggleExpanded` no longer steals focus to the first revealed row on expand, restoring a preview-first model where Enter stays bound to the recommendation; collapsing returns focus to the same recommendation. A `useLayoutEffect` guard forces the list open when `!canCollapse` arrives after mount, and the layout/state mirroring use `useLayoutEffect` to settle state before paint, keeping the landing screen's wordmark promotion in sync.
ai.evidence: The diff in `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx` introduces `showStandaloneRecommended` (true when `!expanded || accessTier === 'limited'`), rewrites `toggleExpanded` to no longer move focus to `otherModels[0]` on expand, adds a guard in the `useLayoutEffect` to force `setExpanded(true)` when `!canCollapse && !expanded`, and changes `renderedModelIds` to omit `recommendedModel.id` from the standalone list when `showStandaloneRecommended` is false so it is not rendered twice in expanded full-access views.
ai.unknowns: The diff shows no change to the public CLI surface or model catalog, so the rollout to end users and any server-side access-tier payload versioning are not visible in this commit.

eli5.text: You are using the free coding assistant on Windows, and after updating to this release it will now run commands through bash instead of the old cmd.exe shell. That matters because Windows systems are set up to use bash for running code, and this change makes the assistant follow that setting instead of falling back to the legacy shell. You can tell because commands will now execute in bash, matching what the system was already configured to use.

facts: Common locations where Git Bash might be installed on Windows Machine-wide Git for Windows layouts. A per-user install (no admin rights) lands under %LOCALAPPDATA% instead, and is found via git.exe below.

WSL bash paths that are often unreliable (VM may not be running, quote escaping issues) These are checked last as a fallback only The WSL launcher ships at C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe whether or not a distro is installed, so it must never be mistaken for a usable bash.
entries.title: SDK update: run-terminal-command

ai.title: SDK drops WSL bash fallback and rewrites Windows bash resolution
ai.summary: The findWindowsBash function in the SDK terminal command tool rewrites Windows bash resolution to check the CODEBUFF_GIT_BASH_PATH override, then GIT_BASH_COMMON_PATHS, then bash.exe/bash on PATH with WSL directories excluded, then bash.exe beside a git.exe on PATH. WSL bash is no longer used as a last resort because it fails with cryptic errors when the VM is not running, on quote escaping, on UTF-16 mismatches, and when no distro is installed. The createWindowsBashNotFoundError message removes the WSL install option, leaving only Git for Windows and the CODEBUFF_GIT_BASH_PATH override as fixes. The find result is built from a flat list of candidates rather than separate loops that deferred WSL paths.
ai.evidence: sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts: the findWindowsBash function is rewritten to check the CODEBUFF_GIT_BASH_PATH env var, GIT_BASH_COMMON_PATHS, bash on PATH (excluding WSL directories matched by WSL_BASH_PATH_PATTERNS), and bash beside a git.exe on PATH, while removing the WSL last-resort fallback. The createWindowsBashNotFoundError message drops the WSL install option, leaving only Git for Windows and CODEBUFF_GIT_BASH_PATH. Comments on GIT_BASH_COMMON_PATHS and WSL_BASH_PATH_PATTERNS are expanded to explain per-user install paths and the System32 bash.exe trap.
ai.unknowns: Whether any existing Windows SDK users relied on the WSL bash fallback that has now been removed entirely.

A new `FREEBUFF_MODEL_PREFERENCE_MIGRATION_ID` of '2026-07-31-v4-flash' triggers `migrateSupersededFreebuffModelPreference` once per user, moving a saved superseded pick to its replacement while still letting a user pin the old choice afterward.

In `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`, `DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_MODEL` gets `displayName: 'DeepSeek V4 Flash 07/31'` and `isNew: true`, `MINIMAX_M3_MODEL` gains a `supersededBy` block pointing to `FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_MODEL_ID`, and `FREEBUFF_WEB_DEEMPHASIZED_MODEL_IDS` now includes `FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_PRO_MODEL_ID`. eli5.text: When you're using an older model that has been replaced by a newer, faster one (like DeepSeek V4 Flash), you'll now see a gentle reminder on the screen telling you the new model is better, but only if that specific older model is the one you're currently looking at. If you switch to viewing a different older model that's also been replaced, you won't see multiple reminders cluttering up the list, just one on the model you're focused on. And if you're already using the recommended new model, you won't see any reminder at all, since there's nothing for you to switch to. This change is live today and only affects what you see in the model selection screen when browsing available models.

ai.summary: Updated `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx` to unconditionally append the ' · Images' suffix to model taglines, removing the `m.multimodal` conditional check. This change ensures every model row displays the image capability indicator, reflecting that text-only models utilize server-side vision substitution (`web/src/llm-api/describe-images.ts`) to process pasted screenshots. The label length calculations (`compactLabelLen`, `fullLabelLen`) were adjusted to always include the 9-character suffix length.

eli5.text: When you open the assistant picker, every model now shows an 'Images' badge next to its name, including text-only models that previously didn't. This reflects that even text-only models can analyze screenshots you paste, using a server-side vision service to read the image first. If you looked, you'd see the badge consistently in both the compact and full model list views. This is live today for anyone using the CLI model selector.
